# `Q-2-33` — Spaces in Link Targets

> Link targets cannot contain spaces. Replace spaces with `%20`, or
> wrap the target in angle brackets: `[text](<my file.png>)`.

## What this means

The URL portion of a link or image — the part inside `(...)` —
cannot contain literal spaces unless it is wrapped in angle
brackets (`<...>`). The standard URL-encoding for a space is `%20`;
an unencoded space terminates the URL prematurely and confuses the
parser.

## Why this happens

Almost always a filename or path with a space character (common
on macOS and Windows):

```markdown
![](image file.png)
```

## How to fix

Wrap the target in angle brackets (CommonMark syntax), which may
contain spaces:

```markdown
![](<image file.png>)
```

or replace each space with `%20`:

```markdown
![](image%20file.png)
```

Both forms produce the same document.

Better still, rename the file so it has no spaces — for example
`image-file.png` or `image_file.png`. URL-encoding works, but
spaces in filenames cause friction in many other tools too.
